content: 1. Resume the enzalutamide dose to the level used prior to initiating the CYP3A4 inducer. 2. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of erdafitinib by altering its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP2C9 or CYP3A4 inducers should not be coadministered with erdafitinib. 3. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ergotamine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin base, erythromycin ethylsuccinate, erythromycin lactobionate, and erythromycin stearate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. 5. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 6. Rifapentine reduces etravirine levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. If etravirine is coadministered with darunavir/ritonavir or saquinavir/ritonavir, rifabutin at 300 mg daily is recommended, but rifapentine is contraindicated. 7. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of everolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of fedratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. The effect of coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer has not been studied. 9. Rifapentine increases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole metabolites (M1 and M2) may increase QT prolongation risks. 10. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Rifapentine reduces fosamprenavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of fruquintinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, continue fruquintinib at the recommended dosage. 14. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ganaxolone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose, but do not exceed the maximum daily dose for weight. 15. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of glasdegib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers. 16. Rifapentine decreases ibrutinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A inducers reduce ibrutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 10-fold. 17. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of idelalisib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease idelalisib systemic exposure. 18. Rifapentine decreases indinavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of infigratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of istradefylline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 22. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ivabradine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 23. Rifapentine reduces ivacaftor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers substantially reduce ivacaftor systemic exposure (~9-fold). 24. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers reduce ivosidenib plasma concentrations. 25. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of ixazomib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong inducers decrease ixazomib Cmax by 54% and AUC by 74%. 26. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, double the larotrectinib dose. Resume the prior dose once the inducer is discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. 27. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of lefamulin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for reduced efficacy if coadministration is unavoidable. 28. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of lenacapavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 30. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of leniolisib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of lovastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of lumateperone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of macimorelin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration may lead to false-positive test results; discontinue strong CYP3A4 inducers and allow sufficient washout time before testing. 35. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of macitentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Rifapentine decreases mestranol levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This may result in contraceptive failure. 37. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of midostaurin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease midostaurin concentrations, reducing efficacy. 38. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of naldemedine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of nefazodone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Rifapentine decreases nelfinavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 41. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of neratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 42. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4; avoid use in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. 43. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). 46. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and norethindrone transdermal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects. 47. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of olaparib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 48. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of olutasidenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers reduce olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. 49. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of osimertinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use with strong CYP3A inducers. 52. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ozanimod by affecting CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP2C8 inducers reduce the exposure of ozanimod’s active metabolites, potentially decreasing efficacy. 53. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of palbociclib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A inducers decrease palbociclib plasma exposure by approximately 85%. 54. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of palovarotene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 55. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of pemigatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of perampanel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased perampanel dose may be needed when coadministered. 57. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of pexidartinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 58. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the pirtobrutinib dose to 300 mg daily (if the dose is 200 mg daily) or increase the dose by 50 mg (if the current dose is 50 mg or 100 mg daily). 59. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of pomalidomide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 60. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ponatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk of ponatinib underexposure. Monitor for signs of reduced efficacy. 61. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of pralsetinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of coadministration with a strong CYP3A inducer. Resume the previous dose after the inducer has been discontinued for at least 14 days. 62. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of praziquantel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 63. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of pretomanid by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate; avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 64. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel and micronized progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised.
